name: Google Cloud audit logs
description: Google Cloud audit logs via Pub/Sub, including Workspace login audit: Admin Activity, Data Access and System Event records for Google Cloud, plus Google Workspace login success/failure, as Splunk_TA_google-cloudplatform indexes them.
source: Cloud Audit Logs / LogEntry / AuditLog reference (cloud.google.com/logging); BigQuery audit logs AuditData reference; Workspace Admin console Login Audit Activity Events appendix; field names and CIM aliases as observed in the dev Splunk index (Splunk_TA_google-cloudplatform)

feed.label: Google Cloud audit logs
feed.description: Cloud Audit Logs (Admin Activity, Data Access, System Event) and Google Workspace login audit events, delivered to Splunk over Cloud Pub/Sub by Splunk_TA_google-cloudplatform: who called what Google Cloud or Workspace API, from where, against which resource, and how it came out.

publish_time.label: Publish time
publish_time.description: When Pub/Sub's server received the publish call that delivered this record; on every sample here it was computed from the record's own timestamp, not read as an independent delivery time.

insert_id.label: Insert id
insert_id.description: A unique identifier for one log entry, used to deduplicate and order entries that share a logName and timestamp.

log_name.label: Log name
log_name.description: The log's resource name, projects/<project>/logs/<log id> (or organizations/<org>/logs/... on auth); the <log id> segment names the audit log type (activity, data_access, system_event).

event_time.label: Event time
event_time.description: The time the audited operation itself happened, as the source recorded it.

receive_time.label: Receive time
receive_time.description: The time Cloud Logging received the entry; an output-only field the system sets, not the caller.

severity.label: Severity
severity.description: Cloud Logging's standard severity level for the entry.

method_name.label: Method name
method_name.description: The specific API method invoked; the field this pack uses to tell one kind of audit record from another.

service_name.label: Service name
service_name.description: The Google Cloud (or Workspace) service that generated the audit log entry.

principal_email.label: Principal email
principal_email.description: The email address of the principal (user, service account or system actor) that made the request.

caller_ip.label: Caller IP
caller_ip.description: The IP address of the caller, as the receiving service saw it; can also read a placeholder like "private" for an internal call.

caller_user_agent.label: Caller user agent
caller_user_agent.description: The user agent string the caller supplied with the request.

resource_name.label: Resource name
resource_name.description: The full path of the Google Cloud (or Workspace organization) resource the operation acted on.

request_resource.label: Request resource
request_resource.description: The resource path named inside the API request body itself; observed on SetIamPolicy, where the AuditLog's shared resourceName field is not populated and the request object names the project instead.

resource_type.label: Resource type
resource_type.description: The monitored resource type that produced the entry: which kind of Google Cloud resource this is, by Cloud Monitoring's resource taxonomy.

project_id.label: Project id
project_id.description: A Google Cloud project id. The same concept names the log's own project, a BigQuery job's project, and a BigQuery table's project; see the project_id_family hazard before assuming one query only touches one project.

instance_id.label: Instance id
instance_id.description: The Compute Engine instance's numeric id, a gce_instance monitored-resource label.

zone.label: Zone
zone.description: The Compute Engine zone the instance runs in, a gce_instance monitored-resource label.

operation_id.label: Operation id
operation_id.description: An arbitrary identifier shared by every log entry that is part of the same long-running operation.

status_message.label: Status message
status_message.description: The operation's own human-readable status text, when the API set one.

cim_action.label: CIM action
cim_action.description: The TA's own coarse classification of what happened to the resource: modified, success, failure or unknown. Computed from the record, not copied from a single source field.

cim_status.label: CIM status
cim_status.description: The TA's CIM status field. Read 'success' on every sample in this pack regardless of what happened; see the status_constant hazard.

iam_role.label: IAM role
iam_role.description: The IAM role a policy binding grants or revokes, for example roles/logging.privateLogViewer.

iam_member.label: IAM member
iam_member.description: The principal a policy binding names, in IAM's type:identifier form, for example user:user@example.com.

iam_delta_action.label: IAM delta action
iam_delta_action.description: Whether this policyDelta entry added or removed the binding.

bq_job_id.label: BigQuery job id
bq_job_id.description: The BigQuery job's own id, unique within its project and location.

bq_query_text.label: BigQuery query text
bq_query_text.description: The SQL text of the query the job ran.

bq_statement_type.label: BigQuery statement type
bq_statement_type.description: The kind of SQL statement the query job ran, for example SELECT.

bq_query_priority.label: BigQuery query priority
bq_query_priority.description: Whether the query ran at interactive or batch priority.

bq_create_disposition.label: BigQuery create disposition
bq_create_disposition.description: Whether the job is allowed to create the destination table if it does not already exist.

bq_write_disposition.label: BigQuery write disposition
bq_write_disposition.description: What the job does to the destination table's existing data: truncate, append or require it be empty.

bq_job_state.label: BigQuery job state
bq_job_state.description: The job's own lifecycle state: pending, running or done.

bq_dataset_id.label: BigQuery dataset id
bq_dataset_id.description: A BigQuery dataset id, either the query's destination dataset or one it read from.

bq_table_id.label: BigQuery table id
bq_table_id.description: A BigQuery table id, either the query's destination table or one it read from.

bq_bytes_processed.label: BigQuery bytes processed
bq_bytes_processed.description: The number of bytes the query scanned.

bq_bytes_billed.label: BigQuery bytes billed
bq_bytes_billed.description: The number of bytes BigQuery billed for the query, rounded up to its billing quantum.

login_event_name.label: Login event name
login_event_name.description: The Workspace Reports API event name for the login attempt, for example login_success.

login_type.label: Login type
login_type.description: The kind of credential the user presented to authenticate.

cim_authentication_method.label: CIM authentication method
cim_authentication_method.description: The TA's own authentication-method field. Read 'unknown' on the loginFailure sample despite a login_type of google_password on the same record; see the auth_method_mismatch hazard.

google:gcp:pubsub:audit:admin_activity.description: Admin Activity audit logs delivered over Cloud Pub/Sub, as Splunk_TA_google-cloudplatform indexes the envelope: user-driven API calls that change a resource's configuration or metadata.
google:gcp:pubsub:audit:admin_activity.note: Always on; cannot be disabled. The AuditLog sits at data.protoPayload; the TA also writes its own CIM alias fields (action, dest, user, vendor_account, ...) alongside the dotted JSON paths.

google:gcp:pubsub:audit:data_access.description: Data Access audit logs delivered over Cloud Pub/Sub: API calls that read a resource's configuration or metadata, and calls that create, modify or read user-provided data such as a BigQuery query.
google:gcp:pubsub:audit:data_access.note: Off by default for most services except BigQuery, where it is always on. Google Workspace login events are also Data Access audit logs at the API level but this TA indexes them to google:gsuite:pubsub:audit:auth instead; see the gsuite_routes_to_data_access hazard.

google:gcp:pubsub:audit:system_event.description: System Event audit logs delivered over Cloud Pub/Sub: entries Google Cloud systems and managed service agents write when they change a resource's configuration without direct user action, for example a live VM migration.
google:gcp:pubsub:audit:system_event.note: Always on; cannot be disabled. Carries data.operation to tie together every entry of one system-driven operation.

google:gsuite:pubsub:audit:auth.description: Google Workspace login audit events (login.googleapis.com) delivered over Cloud Pub/Sub: sign-in successes and failures against a Workspace organization.
google:gsuite:pubsub:audit:auth.note: See the gsuite_routes_to_data_access hazard: Google's own docs class these as Data Access audit logs, but the TA gives them a separate sourcetype from google:gcp:pubsub:audit:data_access.

index_time_ok_false.text: All four containers carry index_time_ok: false in this pack's own sample metadata; correlate on the record's own timestamp field, not on Splunk's _indextime.

clock_family.text: publish_time, data.timestamp, data.receiveTimestamp and (on auth) activityId.timeUsec each mark a different moment; in every sample here publish_time was arithmetically derived from data.timestamp rather than an independent Pub/Sub delivery time, so they move together in this pack's samples, not necessarily in production.

id_family.text: insertId, operation.id, activityId.uniqQualifier, jobName.jobId and resource.labels.instance_id each identify a different thing: a log entry, a long-running operation, a Workspace activity, a BigQuery job, a VM. The same event can carry more than one and they never interchange.

project_id_family.text: project_id appears in resource.labels (the log's own project), jobName (the job's project) and destinationTable/referencedTables (the query's project); a cross-project BigQuery query carries three different values under the same concept.

gsuite_routes_to_data_access.text: Google's own Workspace audit log documentation classifies login.googleapis.com events as Data Access audit logs, and both auth samples' logName ends %2Fdata_access; the TA nonetheless indexes them to google:gsuite:pubsub:audit:auth, a sourcetype distinct from google:gcp:pubsub:audit:data_access. A pivot for 'all Data Access audit logs' must name this sourcetype explicitly; logName's suffix will not select it.

auth_method_mismatch.text: authentication_method read 'unknown' on the loginFailure sample even though login_type was google_password on the same record; treat login_type, not authentication_method, as the source of truth for how the user authenticated.

status_constant.text: The CIM status field read 'success' on every sample in this pack, including the SetIamPolicy, BigQuery job and system_event records; it is not a failure signal here. Use cim_action, or for auth the login_success/login_failure event name, instead.

vendor_product_constant.text: vendor_product ('GCP Identity Access Management') and change_type ('AAA') read the same literal value on every sample across admin_activity, data_access and system_event regardless of the actual service or record type; left unbound rather than asserting a per-event meaning neither field earns.

member_prefix_stripped.text: On admin_activity, the CIM object and object_id fields carry the member's bare identity (user@example.com); the IAM binding's own member field keeps the type prefix (user:user@example.com). Same identity, different string.
